notes: Step E: Metal GPU backend (`aot-llm compile --gpu metal`). The *_metal binaries run the transformer on the GPU: weights mapped zero-copy from the executable's own section, activations and KV cache shared with the CPU, one command buffer per token with 8 dispatches per layer (RoPE, the SwiGLU product and the residual adds fused into the quantized matrix products), and prompt batches as a simdgroup-matrix GEMM. The other two binaries are the same models compiled without a GPU backend, as a control; all four have the benchmark's system prompt baked in. Startup of the GPU binaries includes Metal initialisation (device, kernels from the OS shader cache, mapping the weights); the first run on a machine also compiles the kernels (~0.3 s) and is not shown. Cold first token for the GPU binaries includes paging the weights in through the GPU mapping. Decode on the GPU is bound by the matrix-vector kernels (75-107 GB/s against llama.cpp's ~115 GB/s on this chip). The CPU control binaries ran while other processes still loaded the machine (15-minute load average 15; their decode is 70-79 tok/s against 113-128 in entries 5-6), so compare the GPU columns with the earlier entries rather than with the control rows of this one.
